text:
The Islanders scored twice in 53 seconds late in the first period and then spent a good chunk of the night hanging on while Vancouver took over the middle of the game. Kyle Palmieri tipped in the first goal at 14:57, and Matias Maccelli made it 2-0 at 15:50. Both came at even strength on low-percentage chances (8 and 12 percent), so New York cashed in early on shots that rarely go in.

Vancouver then played the better hockey for 20 minutes. The Canucks out-created the Islanders 1.78 to 0.86 in expected goals in the second, and Max Sasson cut the lead at 7:52. Brock Boeser tied it on the power play at 18:55, a 65 percent chance. Ilya Sorokin finished 1.61 goals better than expected, which kept the damage to two, and the Canucks went 1 for 4 on the power play while New York went 0 for 3.

Then the pattern flipped. New York owned the third, 1.77 to 0.84 in expected goals, and Palmieri put it away at 5:38 on a 60 percent chance, set up by Maccelli and Matthew Schaefer. Overall it was close to a coin flip. The Islanders had 3.68 expected goals to Vancouver's 3.61, and they deserved to win in 51 percent of simulated replays. The Canucks held an edge at even strength (2.15 to 2.64 is the Islanders' lead, actually), so the margin was thin either way, and Palmieri's two goals decided it.
